status: Anya-approved schema, fixtures, and failure semantics. Approval covers this document and the browser consumer that implements it. It does not approve a vendor connection, credential, scheduled transfer, retention exception, or deployment.
purpose: Supply the denominator of local AI spend per delivery: how many releases a team recorded as completed inside a declared period, and how much that count can be trusted.

consumer.transport: file chosen with a file input; read with the local Blob text API

snapshot.source_instance_id: psn_ plus 16 to 64 identifier characters; withheld by the consumer
snapshot.generated_at: RFC 3339 timestamp on a real calendar date; freshness only, never ordering
snapshot.period: period_start and period_end are ISO calendar dates forming a half-open range

record.delivery_id: psn_ plus 16 to 64 identifier characters; withheld by the consumer
record.revision: integer of 1 or more; the greatest revision for a delivery wins
record.version_label: optional; at most 64 characters of a short release name, and never derived from a withheld identifier

identifier_derived_label_rule.normalization: case folded; every non-alphanumeric character removed from both sides before comparison
identifier_derived_label_rule.test: A version label sharing any contiguous run of 3 or more alphanumeric characters with any withheld identifier is identifier-derived.
identifier_derived_label_rule.outcome: identifier_derived_label — the whole document is refused as a privacy violation and no count is taken from it.
identifier_derived_label_rule.why_containment_is_insufficient: Neither normalized string need contain the other for a fragment to be published in order: id ABCDEF123456 with version label "build DEF123" shares def123 while passing every containment test.
identifier_derived_label_rule.second_lock: sanitizeDeliveryLabel re-applies the same test at the forwarding boundary, so a label assembled outside the parser is dropped rather than rendered.
identifier_derived_label_rule.diagnostics: A rejection names the run's length and its normalized offset. It never quotes the label, the run, or the identifier.

prohibited_content: release notes, commit messages, descriptions, titles, or any free prose
author, owner, reviewer, committer, or any human identity
branch, commit, diff, repository, URL, host, or IP
credentials, tokens, keys, cookies, or prompt contents

outcomes.accepted: Complete, fresh, every record in period. The count is usable as stated.
outcomes.incomplete: Usable and knowably a floor: partial or stale export, declared omissions, or records quarantined outside the declared period.
outcomes.incompatible: Nothing is derived and no reading is replaced.

failure_behaviour.partial: Independent valid records are counted; absence never deletes and never implies a release did not ship. Outcome: incomplete, code partial_export.
failure_behaviour.stale: Judged against a caller-supplied timestamp, never a clock inside the parser. Past the freshness target the count is labelled lagging rather than refused. Outcome: incomplete, code stale_export. With no timestamp the outcome states freshness_unknown instead of assuming current.
failure_behaviour.malformed: Invalid JSON, a non-envelope top level, an undeclared or prohibited field, a missing required field, an out-of-range value, an impossible calendar date, or a privacy declaration this contract does not accept refuses the whole document. No partial state is built. Outcome: incompatible.
failure_behaviour.reordered: Arrival order is never authority. The greatest revision for a delivery wins whether it arrives first or last; an identical duplicate collapses; two copies at one revision with different content refuse the document as revision_conflict. The result is independent of array order.
failure_behaviour.replayed: A snapshot sequence at or below one the caller has already accepted is an acknowledged replay: outcome incompatible, code stale_replay, and the existing reading is kept unchanged.
failure_behaviour.period_incompatible: A record outside the declared half-open period is quarantined and counted, not silently dropped; if none remain inside, the document is refused as no_release_in_declared_period. A declared period that cannot overlap the billing period being analyzed is refused as period_incompatible_with_spend.

fixtures.location: generated in tests/shiplog-delivery-history.test.js from one base document
fixtures.why_not_committed: Every scenario is one field away from the valid case, so a generated set cannot drift from the schema it is checked against, and the large ones cost no repository bytes.

not_in_scope: any live connection, credential, URL, webhook, upload, or polling schedule
release size, scope, quality, or content
writing anything back to a source instance

versioning.consumer_rule: Exact reviewed versions are allowlisted; an unknown version is refused without guessing (unsupported_version).
versioning.minor: a new optional field or enum value, plus review
versioning.major: a required field, a removal, a rename, an identifier change, a privacy change, or a semantic change

limits: A duplicate JSON key collapses in the browser's parser before validation; the last value wins and no code in the consumer can see the first. Producers must not emit one.
One export is one reading. The parser holds no high-water mark of its own; replay protection is the caller passing back the sequence it last accepted.
